document.title: Rules Governing the Granting of the OIC Affiliated-Institution Status
document.purpose: Establishes the eligibility requirements, application procedures, rights, obligations, suspension, cancellation, and amendment mechanisms for institutions seeking OIC Affiliated-Institution Status.

charter.description: Charter of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation.

summit.description: Summit of Kings and Heads of State and Government of OIC Member States.

affiliated_institution.description: An entity recognized by the Summit or the Council as affiliated to the OIC under Article 25 of the Charter.

member_states.description: All Member States of the OIC.

mandatory_requirements.description: Application must be submitted officially by the host Member State.
Host State must confirm that the institution’s objectives are consistent with the OIC Charter.
Institution’s statute and incorporation documents must align with OIC objectives and principles.
Institution must operate in one or more OIC Member States.
The headquarters must be located in one of the Member States where it operates.

article_6.document: Application Form for Affiliated Institution Status
List of officials and their CVs
Activity and financial records for the last three years

step_2.action: Officially submit the application with endorsement letter.

step_4.action: Circulate application to Member States one month before the Senior Officials’ Meeting.

step_6.action: Seek to adopt a resolution by consensus.

step_7.action: If rejected, may reapply after two years.

rights.description: May be granted observer status by a Council resolution.
May receive voluntary assistance from Member States, Subsidiary Organs, and Specialized Organs.
May be invited to Summit, Council, and other relevant OIC meetings.
May submit notes and proposals to the OIC and participate in deliberations.
May provide activity information for circulation to Member States.
Host States should seek to provide necessary facilities for representatives.
May use the OIC logo with the phrase ‘Organisation of Islamic Cooperation – affiliated institution’ with written approval of the Secretary General.
May be assigned tasks under OIC resolutions and programs.

obligations.description: Must abide by OIC objectives, principles, and resolutions.
Must respect sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity, and common interests of Member States.
Must submit an annual report describing activities and regulatory changes.
Must report how contributions or assistance from Member States or OIC organs were used.
Host State must immediately notify the General Secretariat if the institution is dissolved or loses legal status.

grounds: Failure to submit reports for two consecutive years.
Activities no longer serve OIC Charter objectives.
Institution commits excesses or prejudice against a Member State.
procedure: Institution is notified and given opportunity to address the issue.
Matter is referred to the Council.
Council decides after consultation with concerned State(s).
suspension.end_of_suspension: Council may end suspension when grounds no longer exist.

grounds: Deviation from OIC objectives and governing rules.
Repeated prejudice against a Member State.
Improper use of the OIC logo.
Failure to remedy suspension grounds within two years.

financial_rules.description: Granting affiliated status does not create financial obligations for the General Secretariat, Subsidiary Organs, Specialized Organs, or Member States.

amendments.adoption_method: Same procedure used for adoption of the Rules.

entry_into_force.effective_date: Date of adoption by the Council of Foreign Ministers.

workflow_summary: Host State endorses and submits it.
Member States receive documents before the Senior Officials’ Meeting.
Approved institution gains affiliated status and related rights.
Institution must submit annual activity and financial reports.
Non-compliance may lead to suspension or cancellation.
